newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin - worried tight labor marts may boost prices.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin - worried tight labor marts may boost prices.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chair Alice Rivlin on Wednesday said that there was concern that the tight labor markets may cause a rise in wage and price inflation.

Interviewed on CNBC, Rivlin said that "the worry -- and the Federal Reserve is supposed to worry -- is that with very tight labor markets we could see wages rising more rapidly in the future, more important, prices going up in the future."
But Rivlin said that although the economy is strong, there hasn't been any indication so far that inflation is breaking out.
"The economy is growing strongly, labor markets are certainly tight, but we haven't seen inflation yet," she said.
She said that wage, and more broadly, total compensation growth, had been quite moderate considering how tight labor markets are.
Rivlin added the recent data showed that growth was very strong in the first quarter but "that perhaps the economy is slowing a little bit in the second quarter."
